data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 2 field(s): density higher vs DMSO; 5 observations; candidates: Microtubule destabilizers, Microtubule stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors, Aurora kinase inhibitors

observations.finding: Severe cell loss / detachment vs DMSO. DMSO f_a07adf52fe25 is confluent monolayer of hundreds of spread MCF-7 cells with oval blue nuclei. Treated f_1ec08ca22b01 shows ~3-5 bright rounded cells top-right with >95% of field empty/black. Treated f_513e247a2726 shows ~20-30 cells clustered lower-right, rest black. Consistent with cytotoxicity/mitotic detachment.

DNA (blue in composite) barely visible as distinct channel in treated fields. Where visible, nuclei are small, round, condensed, often overlapped by intense green/red giving yellow/pink/white spot, not the large oval spread blue nuclei of DMSO. No enlarged/multilobed nuclei. This matches measured nuc_major_axis z=-21.5 (23.6 px vs DMSO median 36.1 px) = small/compact nuclei. Only composites available without grayscale DNA to quantify exactly.

Beta-tubulin (green) massively brighter and more heterogeneous/contrast in treated rounded cells. DMSO shows filamentous dim green network throughout cytoplasm. Treated remaining cells show compact intense punctate/balled green-yellow signal with high local contrast, no spread microtubule fibers.

F-actin (red) also brighter and punctate/ contrasted in treated. DMSO shows red cortical stress fibers and cell-cell contacts. Treated shows intense red-yellow foci coincident with rounded cells, high variance.

Mitotic-like morphology in majority of remaining cells: rounded, phase-bright, high tubulin+actin overlap (yellow), condensed chromatin. DMSO mitotic rate ~0.4% morphology. Treated fraction 0.654 is ~150x higher.

notable_cells.why: 3 bright green-yellow rounded mitotic-like cells top-right only remaining; rest of field empty demonstrating cell loss
Cluster of ~10 yellow/red mitotic-like doublets/round cells lower-center with condensed nuclei and no spread morphology
Additional round yellow/green mitotic-like cells with high tubulin intensity and small nuclei

candidate_mechanisms.why: fraction mitotic-like z=159, tub_mean z=103, tub_std z=63, tub_glcm_contrast z=202 + severe cell loss + small rounded bright cells = classic antimitotic/microtubule poison mitotic arrest

same as above - both destabilizers and stabilizers cause mitotic arrest with condensed small nuclei and hyper-intense tubulin aggregates in composites; cannot distinguish without high-res grayscale tubulin
also cause prolonged mitotic arrest with rounded cells and low cell count; would need monochrome tubulin to confirm monopolar spindles
also cause mitotic arrest/high frac_mitotic_like but typically often produce large/ polyploid nuclei - not seen here (nuclei small); less favored but in differential for mitotic arrest

report.uncertainty: Only composites were provided, no separate grayscale DNA/tubulin/actin channels, so spindle structure, DNA condensation, actin fiber morphology cannot be assessed at high resolution. Distinction between microtubule destabilizer vs stabilizer vs Eg5 requires monochrome tubulin and DAPI at 20x+.

data.critique: Do not approve. The atlas (e6) opposes the call: Actin disruptors win NSC 2/4 and Eg5 inhibitors dominate k-neighbours 5/10, while Microtubule stabilizers have only 1/10 neighbours. Microscopy does not override this: e7 explicitly cannot separate stabilizers, destabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors from composites, and e8's bright/bundled tubulin can be secondary to mitotic rounding. At 1-3 uM (e3,e5) actin features are as extreme as tubulin features. The claimed large/polyploid signature reverses at 10-30 uM (e15,e17) while nuc_area falls monotonically (e12). The decisive 10 uM mitotic signal (e4) is a single rep-1 well with only 28 cells (one field: 2 nuclei), and 30 uM (e2) reverses tubulin/actin/mitotic signals. P=0.62 for stabilizers is therefore over-calibrated; Actin/Eg5 explain the ledger at least as well.
data.requested_experiment: Acquire dose index 2 (0.1 uM), replicate 1, then atlas-compare that well. Below the cytotoxic/rounding 1-30 uM range, persistence of bundled-tubulin/mitotic arrest at 0.1 uM would favour a potent microtubule/Eg5 mechanism, whereas primary actin loss without mitotic arrest (or loss of phenotype) would favour Actin disruptors / lower potency. This single low-dose well discriminates the leading hypotheses and tests the dose trend.

data.note:
Reflection post-unblinding (s_f0826fee65 = AZ138, BBBC021 Eg5 inhibitors):

Incorrect call: Actin disruptors (p=0.34) vs true Eg5 inhibitors. Initial call was Microtubule stabilizers p=0.62 based on tub_mean z~26-103, frac_mitotic_like z=3.7-159, bundled tubulin in e8. Reviewer correctly noted atlas opposed this: e6/e24 NSC Actin 2/4, k-neighbours Eg5 5/10 vs stabilizers 1/10, and microscopy e7 explicitly could not separate stabilizers/destabilizers/Eg5 from composites. 

Faced with no budget to acquire requested 0.1 uM low-dose discriminator, I over-corrected to the NSC plurality (Actin 0.34 vs Eg5 0.31) rather than the stronger mechanistic neighbour signal. In fact 1uM well w_5868a4e8e5 nearest was Eg5 (similarity 0.901) and all 5 Eg5 neighbours were the same Eg5 reference compound across doses (e24), consistent with potent KSP inhibition. The actin features (e3 act_std z36, e5 z39) were secondary to mitotic rounding/cortical contraction in Eg5 arrest, not primary actin loss - a known pitfall where actin/tubulin co-increase in rounded mitotics.

High-dose reversal (30uM e2/e23 blank fields, tub_mean z -18, e26 rho -0.2) and 10uM low-n well (28 cells, one field 2 nuclei e4) flagged cytotoxic detachment that should have down-weighted those doses, but low-dose persistence test was unavailable.

Literature check: AZ138 not in PubChem/ChEMBL. Eg5/KIF11 inhibitors cause monopolar spindles and mitotic arrest with diffuse mitotic phenotypes indistinguishable from MT stabilizers in low-resolution composites: seminal monastrol screen PMID 10542155 and K858 Eg5 inhibitor PMID 19351824 describe rounded mitotic arrest with condensed chromatin; PMID 24997502 discusses image-based profiling synergy predictions including anti-mitotics. This matches e4 massive mitotic fraction and e8 bundled tubulin, which in Eg5 case reflects monopolar rosettes rather than taxane bundles.

Lesson: when NSC is split 2/1/1 and composites are non-diagnostic, k-neighbour dominance (5/10 Eg5) plus per

reflection.text:
After unblinding AZ138 as Eg5 inhibitor (verdict: we concluded Actin disruptors p=0.34, truth Eg5, previous submit was Microtubule stabilizers p=0.62) the evidence ledger was mixed and we over-weighted intermediate/high-dose composite morphology and under-weighted the atlas and dose-trend controls.

What got it right:
- The reference atlas both times (e6 and e24 - identical after 4 wells: NSC Actin 2/4 but k-neighbours Eg5 5/10, Actin 3/10, Cholesterol 1/10, Stabilizers only 1/10) was the only quantitative discriminator. The plurality Eg5 kNN vote was stable and directly pointed to truth. We listed it as supporting Eg5 in hypothesis_history step 18 (p=0.12) and step 27 (p=0.31) but did not act on it.
- The microscopist explicitly warned that composites cannot separate the key classes (e7: candidates = Microtubule destabilizers, stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors, Aurora inhibitors - "cannot separate"). That should have downgraded any morphology-based override of the atlas. e8's "bright/bundled tubulin" candidate Stabilizers was cited as support in step 18/27, but the review critique we received was correct: bundled tubulin can be secondary to mitotic rounding, not primary stabilization.
- Literature after unblinding returned 0 hits for 'AZ138 Eg5' (e29, consistent with lookup_compound failures in PubChem/ChEMBL for this internal code) but 3 hits for 'Eg5 KIF11 inhibitor monopolar spindle mitotic arrest phenotype' (e30). The Eg5 phenotype - monopolar spindles, mitotic arrest due to failure of bipolar spindle formation - is what the atlas was detecting (PMID 10542155; PMID 19351824). Our wells did show extreme mitotic-like signal (e4 frac_mitotic_like z=+159.0, tub_glcm_contrast z=+203.0) which is consistent with that, not diagnostic of stabilizers.
What misled us and what we missed:
1. Acquisition choice: from list_available_experiments (e1: 8 doses 0.01-30 uM, 4 wells left) we sampled only 30 uM (e2), 1 uM (e3), 10 uM (e4), 3 uM (e5) - i.e. the top half of the curve, all in the cytotoxic/rounding range. We exhausted budget (0 left at step 27) and could not execute the decisive request_experiment (dose index 2 = 0.1 uM, rep 1, then atlas-compare) to test persistence of mitotic/bundled phenotype at low dose vs primary actin loss. Low-dose discrimination was the intended tie-breaker between potent Eg5/MT vs Actin and we missed it.
2. Over-interpretation of a low-n well: e4 (10 uM) drove our early stabilizer call (hypothesis_history step 18: tub_mean e3/e4/e5 as support). It had only 28 cells measured (vs 772 at 30 uM e2, 356 at 1 uM e3, 469 at 3 uM e5). The reviewer note that this was "one field: 2 nuclei" explains the inflated z-scores (act_glcm_contrast +144.1) and makes e9-e11 dose_response non-significant: tub_mean rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e9/e26), frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e10), cell_count rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e11). We treated a single-replicate spike as dose-consistent.
3. False dose-trend reading: our rationale for stabilizers cited "rising tubulin intensity, mitotic arrest, and large/polyploid nuclei across three doses" but dose_response contradicts this:
 - nuc_area rho=-1.00 p=0 (e12) monotonic decrease 4 doses, opposite expectation for stabilizer/Aurora-induced large nuclei.
 - nuc_solidity rho=-1.00 p=0 (e14) and nuc_eccentricity rho=+1.00 p=0 (e25) show progressive irregular elongation, not round polyploid.
 - frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.60 p=0.4 (e15) and nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e17) reverse at 10-30 uM, as the review stated. Large/DNA content did not persist.
 - act_tub_ratio rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e22) and act_std rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e20), tub_glcm_contrast rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e21) show no positive actin/tubulin trend.
 In short, no significant dose-dependent increase in tubulin or mitotic fraction, and high-dose reversal (e2 at 30 uM: nuc_solidity z=-129.5, act_tub_ratio z=-91.0, 772 cells) indicates toxicity/rounding artifact rather than stabilization.
4. Actin vs tubulin equivalence at mid-dose: e3 and e5 both show actin features as extreme as tubulin (e3 act_std +36.1, act_glcm_contrast +29.5 vs tub_mean +26.4; e5 act_glcm_contrast +42.3 vs tub_mean +29.5). We initially read tub_mean as stabilizer-specific, then flipped to actin disruptors (step 27: Actin 0.34 vs Eg5 0.31, essentially a coin-flip) by overweighting e2's actin ratio collapse and atlas NSC 2/4. Neither weighted feature alone separates Eg5 from actin/MT classes in this Cell Painting composite, which PMIDs using image-based profiling for MOA prediction also note requires multiparametric controls (PMID 24997502).
5. Calibration: P=0.62 for stabilizers (submit 1) was over-calibrated given atlas opposition (1/10 neighbours) and explicit microscopist ambiguity. Second submit 0.34 acknowledged uncertainty but still chose the wrong side of a 0.34 vs 0.31 split where Eg5 had the stronger kNN evidence.

If this were a real lab, we would have: 1) honored the low-dose 0.1 uM +/- 0.01-0.3 uM titration with sufficient replicates, 2) required >100 cells/well for mitotic calls, 3) run high-resolution beta-tubulin/DAPI monochrome to distinguish monopolar (Eg5) PMID 10542155 PMID 19351824 vs bundled bipolar vs fragmented phenotypes, plus p-HH3 flow for G2/M, and reference Eg5 and actin controls, rather than composites alone.

what_was_wrong: Sampled only 1-30 uM, missed 0.1 uM discriminator and exhausted budget
Trusted 10 uM n=28 well e4 with z=+159 mitotic spike
Claimed rising tubulin/polyploid trend opposite to rho=-1.00 nuc_area e12 and reversal e15/e17

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Do not approve. The atlas (e6) opposes the call: Actin disruptors win NSC 2/4 and Eg5 inhibitors dominate k-neighbours 5/10, while Microtubule stabilizers have only 1/10 neighbours. Microscopy does not override this: e7 explicitly cannot separate stabilizers, destabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors from composites, and e8's bright/bundled tubulin can be secondary to mitotic rounding. At 1-3 uM (e3,e5) actin features are as extreme as tubulin features. The claimed large/polyploid signature reverses at 10-30 uM (e15,e17) while nuc_area falls monotonically (e12). The decisive 10 uM mitotic signal (e4) is a single rep-1 well with only 28 cells (one field: 2 nuclei), and 30 uM (e2) reverses tubulin/actin/mitotic signals. P=0.62 for stabilizers is therefore over-calibrated; Actin/Eg5 explain the ledger at least as well.

Requested: Acquire dose index 2 (0.1 uM), replicate 1, then atlas-compare that well. Below the cytotoxic/rounding 1-30 uM range, persistence of bundled-tubulin/mitotic arrest at 0.1 uM would favour a potent microtubule/Eg5 mechanism, whereas primary actin loss without mitotic arrest (or loss of phenotype) would favour Actin disruptors / lower potency. This single low-dose well discriminates the leading hypotheses and tests the dose trend.

## Reflection

After unblinding AZ138 as Eg5 inhibitor (verdict: we concluded Actin disruptors p=0.34, truth Eg5, previous submit was Microtubule stabilizers p=0.62) the evidence ledger was mixed and we over-weighted intermediate/high-dose composite morphology and under-weighted the atlas and dose-trend controls.

What got it right:
- The reference atlas both times (e6 and e24 - identical after 4 wells: NSC Actin 2/4 but k-neighbours Eg5 5/10, Actin 3/10, Cholesterol 1/10, Stabilizers only 1/10) was the only quantitative discriminator. The plurality Eg5 kNN vote was stable and directly pointed to truth. We listed it as supporting Eg5 in hypothesis_history step 18 (p=0.12) and step 27 (p=0.31) but did not act on it.
- The microscopist explicitly warned that composites cannot separate the key classes (e7: candidates = Microtubule destabilizers, stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors, Aurora inhibitors - "cannot separate"). That should have downgraded any morphology-based override of the atlas. e8's "bright/bundled tubulin" candidate Stabilizers was cited as support in step 18/27, but the review critique we received was correct: bundled tubulin can be secondary to mitotic rounding, not primary stabilization.
- Literature after unblinding returned 0 hits for 'AZ138 Eg5' (e29, consistent with lookup_compound failures in PubChem/ChEMBL for this internal code) but 3 hits for 'Eg5 KIF11 inhibitor monopolar spindle mitotic arrest phenotype' (e30). The Eg5 phenotype - monopolar spindles, mitotic arrest due to failure of bipolar spindle formation - is what the atlas was detecting (PMID 10542155; PMID 19351824). Our wells did show extreme mitotic-like signal (e4 frac_mitotic_like z=+159.0, tub_glcm_contrast z=+203.0) which is consistent with that, not diagnostic of stabilizers.
What misled us and what we missed:
1. Acquisition choice: from list_available_experiments (e1: 8 doses 0.01-30 uM, 4 wells left) we sampled only 30 uM (e2), 1 uM (e3), 10 uM (e4), 3 uM (e5) - i.e. the top half of the curve, all in the cytotoxic/rounding range. We exhausted budget (0 left at step 27) and could not execute the decisive request_experiment (dose index 2 = 0.1 uM, rep 1, then atlas-compare) to test persistence of mitotic/bundled phenotype at low dose vs primary actin loss. Low-dose discrimination was the intended tie-breaker between potent Eg5/MT vs Actin and we missed it.
2. Over-interpretation of a low-n well: e4 (10 uM) drove our early stabilizer call (hypothesis_history step 18: tub_mean e3/e4/e5 as support). It had only 28 cells measured (vs 772 at 30 uM e2, 356 at 1 uM e3, 469 at 3 uM e5). The reviewer note that this was "one field: 2 nuclei" explains the inflated z-scores (act_glcm_contrast +144.1) and makes e9-e11 dose_response non-significant: tub_mean rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e9/e26), frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e10), cell_count rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (e11). We treated a single-replicate spike as dose-consistent.
3. False dose-trend reading: our rationale for stabilizers cited "rising tubulin intensity, mitotic arrest, and large/polyploid nuclei across three doses" but dose_response contradicts this:
 - nuc_area rho=-1.00 p=0 (e12) monotonic decrease 4 doses, opposite expectation for stabilizer/Aurora-induced large nuclei.
 - nuc_solidity rho=-1.00 p=0 (e14) and nuc_eccentricity rho=+1.00 p=0 (e25) show progressive irregular elongation, not round polyploid.
 - frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.60 p=0.4 (e15) and nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e17) reverse at 10-30 uM, as the review stated. Large/DNA content did not persist.
 - act_tub_ratio rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e22) and act_std rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e20), tub_glcm_contrast rho=-0.20 p=0.8 (e21) show no positive actin/tubulin trend.
 In short, no significant dose-dependent increase in tubulin or mitotic fraction, and high-dose reversal (e2 at 30 uM: nuc_solidity z=-129.5, act_tub_ratio z=-91.0, 772 cells) indicates toxicity/rounding artifact rather than stabilization.
4. Actin vs tubulin equivalence at mid-dose: e3 and e5 both show actin features as extreme as tubulin (e3 act_std +36.1, act_glcm_contrast +29.5 vs tub_mean +26.4; e5 act_glcm_contrast +42.3 vs tub_mean +29.5). We initially read tub_mean as stabilizer-specific, then flipped to actin disruptors (step 27: Actin 0.34 vs Eg5 0.31, essentially a coin-flip) by overweighting e2's actin ratio collapse and atlas NSC 2/4. Neither weighted feature alone separates Eg5 from actin/MT classes in this Cell Painting composite, which PMIDs using image-based profiling for MOA prediction also note requires multiparametric controls (PMID 24997502).
5. Calibration: P=0.62 for stabilizers (submit 1) was over-calibrated given atlas opposition (1/10 neighbours) and explicit microscopist ambiguity. Second submit 0.34 acknowledged uncertainty but still chose the wrong side of a 0.34 vs 0.31 split where Eg5 had the stronger kNN evidence.

If this were a real lab, we would have: 1) honored the low-dose 0.1 uM +/- 0.01-0.3 uM titration with sufficient replicates, 2) required >100 cells/well for mitotic calls, 3) run high-resolution beta-tubulin/DAPI monochrome to distinguish monopolar (Eg5) PMID 10542155 PMID 19351824 vs bundled bipolar vs fragmented phenotypes, plus p-HH3 flow for G2/M, and reference Eg5 and actin controls, rather than composites alone.

What was right:
- Atlas kNN Eg5 5/10 twice (e6/e24)
- Microscopist warning composites cannot separate classes (e7)

What was wrong or missed:
- Sampled only 1-30 uM, missed 0.1 uM discriminator and exhausted budget
- Trusted 10 uM n=28 well e4 with z=+159 mitotic spike
- Claimed rising tubulin/polyploid trend opposite to rho=-1.00 nuc_area e12 and reversal e15/e17

Proposed next experiment: Not clinical. Low-dose titration 0.01-0.3 uM with n>2 replicates/well, high-res tubulin/DAPI + actin phalloidin, centrin/gamma-tubulin for monopolar vs bipolar, p-HH3 quant; compare to validated Eg5 inhibitor and actin disruptor references.
